I've been farming for just two years, so I mostly watch what my neighbors do and follow the village pattern. I'm 61 now — my back gives me trouble and my son works in the city, so my wife and I handle most of the field work ourselves. I can't afford to experiment or take risks. The land is 7.7 mu and both crops run on the same plots, rotating.

For **wheat**: I plant in October after maize harvest. I'll do rotary tillage — a neighbor lends me his machine — and use an improved variety the seed shop recommends, not old seed. I'll apply compound fertilizer at planting and urea at jointing. I'm not precise about the amounts; I go by the bag labels and what the village technician told me once. I irrigate at sowing, jointing, and heading — three times is what everyone here does. I spray herbicide in winter and a fungicide before heading because stripe rust hurt people's fields last year.

For **maize**: I plant right after wheat harvest in June, usually with a seeder the village cooperative has. I use hybrid seed because yields are better — even I know that. Fertilizer goes in at planting and again at V6 or so. Summer rain usually helps but I pump once if July goes dry. I spray for fall armyworm because it's been bad lately.

I keep inputs modest — I'm not running a big operation and every yuan I spend I feel it.
